aubergine.$description: Aubergine — Page canvas, hero backgrounds, nav background — the single dominant surface color that gives Front its unmistakable identity

royal-plum.$description: Royal Plum — Pink supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

lime-spark.$description: Lime Spark — Green supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

bright-violet.$description: Bright Violet — Violet supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

lavender-glow.$description: Lavender Glow — Decorative borders, accent strokes on illustrations, gradient terminus in the chat widget

ink.$description: Ink — Primary body and heading text on light surfaces — near-black with a faint warm cast

frost.$description: Frost — Light supporting surface for subtle backgrounds and section separation. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

pale-lilac.$description: Pale Lilac — Light supporting surface for subtle backgrounds and section separation. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

stone.$description: Stone — Borders on light surfaces, table dividers, inactive outlines

slate.$description: Slate — Secondary text, helper copy, metadata labels

pewter.$description: Pewter — Tertiary text, placeholder copy, disabled labels

ash.$description: Ash — Supporting neutral for secondary UI, dividers, and muted labels. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

midnight-navy.$description: Midnight Navy — Violet supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

lavender-whisper.$description: Lavender Whisper — Inset focus ring color, soft hover wash, tinted shadow on elevated cards

deep-olive.$description: Deep Olive — Rare dark text accent on the lime button and light surfaces with maximum contrast

suisse-intl.$description: Primary typeface across all UI — body, headings, buttons, navigation. The custom neo-grotesque gives Front its machined, Swiss-instrument feel; weight 500 carries both body and display, so the system relies on tracking and size to create hierarchy rather than weight contrast.

suisse-works.$description: Rare serif accent — appears as a single contextual flourish, not a structural face
